output.answer: As of November 2026, "Celsius" spans two different companies. At Celsius Holdings (NASDAQ: CELH, the energy-drink maker), a federal securities-fraud class action was filed Nov. 3, 2026 in the Southern District of Florida (26-cv-62465, class period Feb. 21, 2025-June 3, 2026) alleging the company concealed the cardiac risks of its Alani Nu drinks, which it bought for $1.65 billion in April 2025; that follows an April 2026 wrongful-death suit against Alani Nu distributors, a June 4, 2026 Texas attorney-general investigation, and consumer "healthwashing" class actions filed Oct. 26 and Oct. 28, 2026 over the brand's "accelerates metabolism" and "burns body fat" claims. At the bankrupt crypto lender Celsius Network, founder Alex Mashinsky was sentenced May 8, 2025 to 12 years in prison after pleading guilty to securities and commodities fraud, and in 2026 the CFTC resolved its 2023 case with a consent order imposing permanent trading and registration bans while New York's attorney general secured up to $35 million from him plus a permanent industry ban. Celsius Network's bankruptcy litigation also includes its clawback suit against Tether over a ~$4 billion Bitcoin liquidation (most claims survived dismissal in July 2025), a settled ~$517 million clawback suit against FTX's Bahamas unit, a settled creditors'-committee class action that sought $5.2 billion over management misconduct, and a ruling that customers worldwide who withdrew more than $100,000 pre-bankruptcy face US clawback suits.
caveats: "Celsius" is ambiguous: the litigation above involves two distinct companies — Celsius Holdings, Inc. (energy drinks, NASDAQ: CELH) and the defunct crypto lender Celsius Network LLC. If the user means only one of them, the other set of cases is out of scope.

The retrieved pages do not state the dates of the FTX clawback settlement, the customer-clawback jurisdiction ruling, or the dismissed PepsiCo-partnership investor suit, so their timing cannot be pinned down.
The $16.5 million FTC payment by Celsius founders/executives is reported in the New York AG press release rather than in an FTC release, so the figure is secondhand here.
The Tether clawback case remains open (one claim dismissed, others headed toward trial), and the outcome of the $4 billion transfer claims is uncertain.

The November 2026 securities class action and the October 2026 consumer class actions are newly filed allegations only; nothing has been tested in court, and Celsius has said it stands by its peer-reviewed studies and product claims.

passages.quote: NEW YORK, Nov. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Pomerantz LLP announces that a class action lawsuit has been filed against Celsius Holdings, Inc. ("Celsius" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: CELH) and certain officers.   The class action, filed in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, and docketed under 26-cv-62465, is on behalf of a class consisting of all persons and entities other than Defendants that purchased or otherwise acquired Celsius securities between February 21, 2025 and June 3, 2026, both dates inclusive (the "Class Period"), seeking to recover damages caused by Defendants' violations of the federal securities laws and to pursue remedies under Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5 promulgated thereunder, against the Company and certain of its top officials.

The truth began to emerge on April 9, 2026, when NBC News and local news outlet MyRGV (Rio Grande Valley) reported that the family of 17-year old Texas cheerleader Larissa Rodriguez had filed a wrongful death lawsuit in Hidalgo County District Court against Glazer's Beer and Beverage, LLC ("Glazer's") and Glazer's Beer and Beverage of Texas, LLC, two distributors of Alani Nu. The family alleged that Rodriguez died from an enlarged heart caused by drinking Alani Nu energy drinks and that the drinks "had inadequate warnings about the serious cardiac risks" of drinking Alani Nu. According to NBC News, Celsius stated in response, _inter alia_, "our policy is not to market or sample to anyone under 18".

Then, on June 4, 2026, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton ("Paxton") announced an investigation into Celsius over concerns that its high-caffeine energy drinks are being marketed to children and teens. Per Attorney General Paxton's announcement, the investigation will specifically examine whether Celsius and its Alani Nu subsidiary had violated the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act by misrepresenting the safety of their products.

NEW YORK, May 8 (Reuters) - [Alex Mashinsky](https://www.reuters.com/technology/who-is-alex-mashinsky-man-behind-alleged-celsius-crypto-fraud-2023-01-05/), the founder and former chief executive of bankruptcy cryptocurrency lender Celsius Network, was sentenced on Thursday to 12 years in prison after [pleading guilty](https://www.reuters.com/technology/celsius-founder-alex-mashinsky-intends-plead-guilty-two-fraud-counts-2024-12-03/) in December to securities fraud and commodities fraud.

Mashinsky sought one year and one day in prison, saying he felt remorse and wanted to do right by his family and former Celsius customers. His sentence includes three years of supervised release and a $48.4 million forfeiture.

**WASHINGTON** — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York entered a consent order that resolves the CFTC’s 2023 enforcement action against **Alexander Mashinsky**, the founder and former CEO of Celsius Network LLC. \[See CFTC Press Release No. [8749-23](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/8749-23)\]. The consent order permanently enjoins Mashinsky from further violations of certain anti-fraud provisions in the CEA and CFTC regulations and imposes permanent trading and registration bans against him.

On July 11, 2023, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York filed a parallel criminal action against Mashinsky in connection with the same conduct at issue in the CFTC’s action. _USA v. Alexander Mashinsky_, No. 1:23-cr-00347-JGK (S.D.N.Y. July 11, 2023). On Dec. 3, 2024, Mashinsky pled guilty to one count of commodities fraud and one count of securities fraud. On May 8, 2025, Mashinsky was sentenced to 12 years in prison and ordered to pay a $50,000 fine and forfeiture of $48,393,446 for committing commodities fraud and securities fraud at Celsius.

NEW YORK – New York Attorney General Letitia James today [announced that she has secured up to $35 million from Alex Mashinsky,](https://ag.ny.gov/sites/default/files/settlements-agreements/new-york-v-alex-mashinsky-stipulation-2026.pdf) a co-founder and former CEO of cryptocurrency lending platform Celsius Network LLC (Celsius), as well as a permanent ban on his participation in the securities, commodities, and cryptocurrency industries. Attorney General James [sued Mashinsky in 2023](https://ag.ny.gov/press-release/2023/attorney-general-james-sues-former-ceo-celsius-cryptocurrency-platform-defrauding) for defrauding hundreds of thousands of investors, including more than 26,000 in New York, by misleading them about Celsius’ safety to encourage them to deposit billions of dollars in digital assets onto his platform. Celsius lost hundreds of millions of dollars on risky investments, which Mashinsky attempted to hide from investors. Mashinsky also failed to register as a salesperson for Celsius and as a securities and commodities dealer, in violation of New York law. The eventual collapse of Celsius left many investors in financial ruin.

output.question: What lawsuits involve Celsius?

key_facts.fact: A federal securities class action was filed against Celsius Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: CELH) and certain officers in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida, docketed 26-cv-62465, on behalf of purchasers of Celsius securities between Feb. 21, 2025 and June 3, 2026.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced an investigation into Celsius over marketing of high-caffeine energy drinks (including its Alani Nu subsidiary) to children and teens, examining possible violations of the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act.

The family of 17-year-old Texas cheerleader Larissa Rodriguez filed a wrongful-death lawsuit in Hidalgo County District Court against Alani Nu distributors Glazer's Beer and Beverage, LLC and Glazer's Beer and Beverage of Texas, LLC, alleging she died from an enlarged heart caused by drinking Alani Nu energy drinks.

New York Attorney General Letitia James secured up to $35 million from former Celsius CEO Alex Mashinsky and a permanent ban on his participation in the securities, commodities and cryptocurrency industries, settling her 2023 fraud lawsuit.

Over $3.4 billion had been distributed to Celsius creditors in the company's bankruptcy as of August 2026; separately, Celsius founders and executives were forced to pay $16.5 million to the Federal Trade Commission.

The CFTC announced a consent order resolving its 2023 enforcement action against Alexander Mashinsky, permanently enjoining him from further anti-fraud violations and imposing permanent trading and registration bans.

Alex Mashinsky, founder and former CEO of Celsius Network, was sentenced to 12 years in prison by U.S. District Judge John Koeltl after pleading guilty in December 2024 to securities fraud and commodities fraud; the sentence includes three years of supervised release and a $48.4 million forfeiture.

Celsius Network's clawback suit against Tether — potentially worth at least $4 billion over Tether's 2022 liquidation of roughly 39,500-40,000 Bitcoin pledged as loan collateral — survived a dismissal attempt, with the transfer claims ordered to trial and only one claim dismissed.

Bankrupt Celsius Network proposed paying 5% more (potentially 105% payout) to many account holders who opt into settling the unsecured creditors' committee's proposed class action seeking at least $5.2 billion and accusing Celsius of fraud and misrepresentation by management.
FTX's Bahamas unit and Celsius Network reached a settlement resolving an adversary lawsuit seeking the return of around $517 million in pre-bankruptcy transfers.

A New York bankruptcy judge (Judge Martin Glenn) ruled that Celsius Network customers worldwide who withdrew more than $100,000 just before the collapse are subject to clawback litigation in the US, including thousands who declined prior settlement offers.

Celsius Holdings Inc. and top executives defeated a securities investor lawsuit alleging they misrepresented inventory levels and demand after the PepsiCo distribution deal; the S.D. Fla. court found insufficient allegations of scienter against each executive.

Consumer class actions accusing Celsius of "healthwashing" — misleading "accelerates metabolism" and "burns body fat" label claims — were filed Oct. 28, 2026 in the N.D. Ill. (Nielsen v. Celsius) and Oct. 26, 2026 in the W.D. Wash.
